title: Card-on-File Terms — Card Use and the Good-Faith Percentage of a Final-Notice Paydown
content:
**Term.** The good-faith percentage of a final-notice paydown on the Patient Financial Account is lowered by 10 points when a card-on-file payment was posted to the account within the one calendar month before the handling date, by 5 points when no such payment was posted but the account holds a card on file, and by nothing otherwise.

| Card-on-file payment posted within 1 calendar month | Account holds a card on file | Good-faith percentage lowered by |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes or no | 10 points |
| no | yes | 5 points |
| no | no | nothing |

**Reading the records.**

- A card-on-file payment is a payment entry on the account ledger received through the card on file; its posting date decides whether it falls within the month.
- "Holds a card on file" is what the account record shows about a card kept on file.
- The one-month window ends on the handling date and reaches back one calendar month, a date on the same calendar day one month earlier falling outside it. On a handling date of 18 August, a card-on-file payment posted on 19 July is within the month; one posted on 18 July is not.

**Hypothetical example.** An account holding a card on file whose last card-on-file payment was posted seven weeks before the handling date: the percentage is lowered by 5 points. Had that payment been posted three weeks before, it would be lowered by 10 points.
